description: Greenhouse pot experiment, Yaqui Valley (Sonora, Mexico): two tomato cultivars (Amalia salt-tolerant, Claudia salt-susceptible) each with three treatments T1 saline soil ECse 6 dS m-1 without QuitoMax, T2 nonsaline soil ECse 0.98 dS m-1 + QuitoMax 300 mg L-1 foliar, T3 saline soil + QuitoMax; completely randomized design, unifactorial arrangement, varieties analysed separately; 5 plants per replicate, n=15 plants per treatment (Table captions); no nonsaline untreated control.
system: greenhouse pots, 4.63 kg vertisol-type soil per pot, Instituto Tecnologico del Valle del Yaqui, Sonora, Mexico

description: Growth-room pot experiment, Solanum lycopersicum cv. Micro-Tom, 1.5 L pots (pits:vermiculite 3:1), ~26 C, ~65 % RH, 16 h photoperiod, LED. 2x2 factorial: foliar Ascophyllum nodosum formulation (SuperFifty Prime, 0.4 % v/v, ~12 ml/plant, 7 and 1 days before pollination) vs water spray x drought (watering withheld from pollination day; ~50 % SFC at 6 DAP, ~25 % SFC at 11 DAP; rewatered 11 DAP, recovery 13 DAP) vs well watered (~96 % SFC). Nine pots per treatment (Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 captions).

In vitro assay (Sec. 2.2.1): cv. Riccio of Parma seedlings in sterilized glass pots (10 cm diameter, 8 cm high) on 1/2 MS + 1% sucrose + 1% plant agar, 4 plants per pot, growth chamber 24 C, 16/8 h, 120 umol m-2 s-1. After first true leaf, roots dipped 15 min in 20 mL PVr_9 suspension (1e8 cells/mL) or not, then transferred to 1/2 MS with or without 150 mM NaCl. 2x2 factorial (Control; PVr_9; 150 mM NaCl; PVr_9 + 150 mM NaCl). Molecular sampling at 72 h (n=3 biological replicates); morphology/fresh weight after five days (15 plants per treatment). No dry biomass or fruit endpoint.

Greenhouse/growth-chamber pot experiment (Sec. 2.2.2, 3.2): sterilized horticultural soil, 0.1 L pots (4.5 cm wide, 5.5 cm high), 24 C, 52 days. Three weeks after germination, 15 mL PVr_9 suspension (1e8 cells/mL) added to the soil of each pot once a week for three weeks (water on remaining days); then 15 mL 150 mM NaCl or water three times a week. 2x2 factorial (CNT; PVr_9; 150 mM NaCl; 150 mM NaCl + PVr_9), two-way ANOVA + Tukey. Endpoints: shoot fresh weight (Fig. 3B), shoot dry weight at 65 C (Fig. 3C, target DRY_BIOMASS shoot), chlorophyll, proline, sugars, APX, CAT, leaf minerals (Table S1). Captions n = 4 biological replicates; Methods 2.3 states 15 plants per treatment; experiment replicated twice.

Open-field pot experiment (Sec. 2.2.3, 3.3): seedlings raised in 0.1 L pots of sterilized soil in greenhouse, inoculated or not with 15 mL PVr_9 (1e8 cells/mL) once a week for three weeks starting three weeks after germination, then transplanted to 4-L pots of horticultural soil in the field, one plant per pot, three plants (replicates) per treatment. From ten days after beginning of flowering (one month after transplanting), half of inoculated and uninoculated plants received 10 NaCl applications, one every three days (50 mM, 100 mM, then 8 x 150 mM; 1 L per pot); controls received the same water volume. 2x2 factorial. Mature fruits harvested at end of trial for composition only (dry matter, soluble solids, ashes, minerals, antioxidants; Fig. 5, Fig. 6, Table S2); no fruit-yield mass or plant biomass reported.

Pot trial under tunnel, Portici (Naples, Italy), spring-summer 2023: cherry tomato cv. Tomito F1 in 65 L pots (sandy soil); 4 irrigation-water salinity levels (EC0 tap water 0.3 dS m-1, EC3, EC6, EC9 dS m-1 by NaCl) x 2 biostimulant levels (untreated vs Enerleaf Ascophyllum nodosum extract foliar 3 L ha-1 equivalent, 3 bi-weekly applications from 31 March); split-plot (salinity main plot, biostimulant sub-plot), 3 replicate pots per cell, 24 pots; single end-of-cycle harvest.

Greenhouse open hydroponic (perlite bag) tomato experiment, Athens 2022: 2 Greek landraces x 2 NaCl levels (0.5 vs 30 mM in nutrient solution from transplanting) x 3 foliar biostimulant treatments (control, A. nodosum 'Algastar' 2 mL/L, PGPR 'Nitrostim' 5 mL/L; 1 week after transplanting then every 15 days); RCBD, 4 bags x 3 plants per treatment, 144 plants; cumulative yield over harvests 1 June to crop termination.
system: Greenhouse, open soilless hydroponic system, perlite bags (Geoflor Hydro), drip-fed nutrient solution

description: Hydroponic greenhouse seedling experiment (14 h light, 26/20 C, 70% RH): tomato seedlings in 1/10 Hoagland solution with 0, 100 or 150 mM NaCl, with or without Na2SiO3 or SiNPs at 100 or 200 mg L-1 in the solution for 20 d; 11 treatments, 3 replicates each; one-way ANOVA/Duncan.

Greenhouse pot experiment (9.5 L pots, river sand, drip fertigation), Experimental Farm 'Nello Lupori', University of Tuscia, Viterbo, spring-summer 2021 (transplant 23 Mar 2021, end 27 Jul 2021 = 123 DAT); cv. Pralyna cherry F1; 2 x 4 randomized complete block factorial: NaCl in nutrient solution (1 vs 50 mM) x biostimulant (Control, PH1, PH2, PH3 foliar 2.5 g/L); 4 replicates of 3 plants per treatment (n=4), 32 experimental units.

Growth-room pot experiment, tomato cv. MicroTom in 2 L pots (compost/vermiculite/perlite 6:1:1), 27/22 C, 16 h light, 80% RH, 120 umol m-2 s-1; 2 x 3 completely randomized block design: Drought (unstressed vs two 14-d water-withholding periods) x Chitosan foliar spray (solvent control, mushroom chitosan MC, crustacean chitosan CC; 0.01% w/v, 3 applications); 8 plants per subgroup; final fruit harvest at 122 d plant age.

Growth-cabinet seedling experiment, tomato cv. Kayra F1 in perlite with Hoagland solution; 3 stress levels (none, 200 mM NaCl 5 d, drought by withholding irrigation 5 d, from end of day 21) fully crossed with 3 bioregulator levels (none, dopamine 100 uM, progesterone 1 uM in Hoagland from sowing to harvest); 9 arms, triplicate x 20 plants; destructive harvest at day 26.
system: growth cabinet; 400 ml containers, sterile perlite, Hoagland solution every other day; 16 h light/8 h dark, 24 C, 50% RH

description: Open-ground field experiment March-June 2024, tomato cv. Rio Fuego in 4 kg soil:tezontle (2:1 v/v) bags, completely randomized design; CTRL, Leonardite hydrolate (L, 1:100), marine Streptomyces sp. LAP3 (MS, 1:10 culture dilution) and MS+L, 250 mL/plant by irrigation at 23, 42 and 73 DAS; 6 plants per treatment; all arms exposed to ambient heatwave/temporary drought (38-40 C) during flowering and fruit development.

Fig 3 (p5): WT Micro-Tom plants sprayed weekly with water (Control) or nano-Se 20 mg/L (foliar, plus fruit spray after fruit set); detached fruits harvested at Br, Br+3 and Br+7, wound-inoculated with Botrytis cinerea agar plugs, lesion diameter (cm) at 72 h; n=6 fruits per bar, mean +/- SD, Student t-test.
system: Greenhouse Micro-Tom (16 h light, 22 C, 60% RH); pre-harvest nano-Se spray; postharvest detached-fruit B. cinerea inoculation assay at 20 C, moist chamber

description: Fig 10a-d (p11) and Results p9: WT Micro-Tom and two SlMYC2 CRISPR/Cas9 knockout lines (axis labels myc2-2, myc2-5; caption/text myc2-5, myc2-7), each mock (H2O) or nano-Se20; fruits at Br, Br+3, Br+7 inoculated with B. cinerea, lesion diameter (cm) at 72 h; n=6 fruits per bar, mean +/- SD. Separate run from E1.
system: Greenhouse Micro-Tom (16 h light, 22 C, 60% RH); nano-Se20 per Methods application protocol; postharvest detached-fruit B. cinerea inoculation assay at 20 C, moist chamber

description: Pot experiment, tomato cv. Pusa Ruby, 15 kg autoclaved sandy loam per pot (30 cm x 40 cm), winter season, ACHR Udheywala Jammu (plastic greenhouse/growth chamber per Methods); completely randomized design with six treatments: well-watered non-inoculated control, drought (soil moisture 8+/-2% vs 35+/-5%), drought + Azotobacter chroococcum, drought + Pseudomonas putida, drought + Bacillus subtilis, drought + 1:1:1 consortium; inoculation by 30 min root dip in ~1e8 CFU/mL before transplanting.

Single greenhouse pot experiment (unheated greenhouse, Milazzo ME, Italy; open soilless system, 5 L black plastic pots 20x20 cm, coconut-fibre substrate, drip fertigation; datterino tomato cv. SV1201TC). Explicit factorial of 2 water regimes (100% vs 50% of crop water requirement [Methods 2.3: 2 vs 1 L h-1]; Methods 2.1 words it as 100 and 50% of container capacity; irrigation treatments initiated 7 days after transplanting) x 3 biostimulant levels (C = equal volume distilled-water spray; D1 = 1.5 g/L Algaren Twin + 3 g/L Drin On; D2 = 2 g/L Algaren Twin + 4 g/L Drin On; foliar spray to leaf runoff, freshly prepared before each application; number/timing of applications not stated) = six treatments. Two-way ANOVA, completely randomized design, three replications per treatment, six plants per replicate (Methods 2.1 p2, 2.2 p2, 2.3 p3, 2.7 p4).

Greenhouse pot experiment, tomato cv. Campbell33, 2x2x2 factorial: NaCl 0 vs 150 mM (ramped 50/100/150 mM weekly from 20 d after AMF inoculation) x green-waste compost (0 vs 5% of soil) x indigenous AMF (autoclaved vs live 20 g inoculum soil); 1 plant per pot, random placement; terminal harvest 3 months after salt application.

Growth-promotion pot experiment without stress (Sec 2.2, Fig 1): tomato cv. Roma in 12-inch pots with 4.5 kg autoclaved soil, greenhouse 14-30 C natural photoperiod; 50 mL B. subtilis IS1 or B. amyloliquefaciens IS6 suspension (OD600 0.5) applied near roots 20 d after emergence, control sterile water; RBD; harvest after six weeks; 5 biological replicates per treatment, repeated twice.

Main multistress pot experiment (Sec 2.5-2.6, Table 1): tomato cv. Roma in 4-inch pots with sterilized silt loam soil, greenhouse; 50 mL soil drench of IS1 or IS6 (OD600 0.1, NaCl-adapted culture) 10 d after emergence, control equal distilled water; 3 d later stress: NaCl 150 mM saline irrigation at 75% field capacity or 50 mL F. oxysporum f.sp. lycopersici conidia (10^3-10^4/mL); seven treatments UC, SS, Fol, SS+IS1, SS+IS6, Fol+IS1, Fol+IS6; no bacteria-alone arm (not a complete S x B factorial); harvest 20 d after treatment application; 10 biological replicates per treatment, repeated twice; one-way ANOVA/Tukey.

In planta greenhouse pot experiment (icipe Duduville, Nairobi): tomato cv. Money-maker, 5 L pots (topsoil:goat manure 5:1, sterile), two seedlings per pot; complete 2x4 crossing of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici soil drench (none vs 10 mL of 1e8 conidia/mL on sowing day) and endophyte seed inoculation (none, T. asperellum M2RT4, T. harzianum KF2R41, H. lixii F3ST1; seeds soaked 18 h in 1e8 conidia/mL); CRD with three replications over time; n=8 per table captions. Outcomes: disease incidence/severity 15-60 dpi, growth 15-60 dpi, root/shoot/whole-plant dry weight, fruit number, single fruit weight, yield kg/plant (Tables 4-5).

Greenhouse pot experiment, tomato cv CastleMart, 2x2 crossed design: water vs Systemin (20 nM final in pot, single substrate application 4 weeks after germination) x non-infected vs Botrytis cinerea CECT2100 spray inoculation (10^6 spores/ml on 3rd and 4th leaves, 24 h after Sys). Endpoints: disease rating 72 hpi and fungal gDNA qPCR 48 hpi (infected arms only), callose 24/48 hpi, starch 6/24 hpi, proteomics/metabolomics 24 hpi, enzyme activities 6/24/48 hpi. Methods pp. 2-5.
system: GREENHOUSE_POT (tunnel-type greenhouse; 200 cm3 pots, vermiculite substrate, Hoagland solution twice weekly)

description: Growth/physiology experiment in uninfected plants: water vs Systemin 20 nM (single treatment); plant height 4, 10 and 15 d after treatment, leaf area 4 and 15 d, leaf fresh and dry weight 15 d after treatment; six individual plants per condition. Methods p. 4-5; data only in Supplementary Fig. S9 (not in corpus).
system: GREENHOUSE_POT (tunnel-type greenhouse; 200 cm3 pots, vermiculite substrate)

description: In planta glasshouse pot experiment (Methods 2.6.1, p4; Data analysis 2.7, p5): tomato cv. PKM1, 25-day-old seedlings transplanted into plastic pots (24 cm diameter) of sterilized red soil:vermicompost:sand (2:1:1). Nine treatments T1-T9 in a completely randomized design; each treatment replicated 10 times (pots) with four plants per pot. Biotic stresses: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. lycopersici isolate TF-N soil inoculation at 5th DAT and/or Meloidogyne incognita 5 mL (2000 motile J2s)/pot at 5th DAT. Biostimulant/biocontrol: Trichoderma asperellum Tv1 conidial suspension (seedling root dip before transplanting per Methods text; soil application 5 mL/pot on 1st and 10th DAT; concentration measured by hemocytometer but not printed). Chemical reference arms: carbendazim 0.1% soil application 10th DAT (T5) and carbofuran 1 g/pot 10th DAT (T7). Single destructive assessment at 30 DPI (uprooting): growth/fresh/dry weight (Table 3, p9), Fusarium wilt incidence (Table 4, p10), nematode variables (Table 5, p11). In vitro dual-culture, crude-metabolite, J2 mortality and egg-hatch assays (Tables 1-2, Figures 3-6) involve no plants and are not mapped as experiments.

Greenhouse pot experiment (evaporative-cooled greenhouse, 15 h day/9 h night, 28 +/- 2 C, RH 42 +/- 5%), tomato cv. Elisa, one plant per pot; root-knot nematode M. incognita 1000 J2/pot at 7 days after transplanting; T1 uninoculated control, T2 nematode only, T3 nematode + endophytic fungus MR20 drench, T4 nematode + bacterial mixture MR12+MR25 drench, T5 nematode + oxamyl; five replicates (1 plant/replicate) in a randomized complete block design (RCBD); assessed once at 60 days after transplanting; authors merged repeated greenhouse trials (Methods p.422; Fig. 5 caption: 10 replicates from two repeated experiments).

In vivo biocontrol vs Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. radicis-lycopersici PVCT127 (Forl, crown and root rot), growth chamber, cv. Moneymaker in 2 L pots. Pathogen-inoculated untreated Control + 10 single-strain endophyte treatments (seed soaking 30 min + 50 mL soil drench of 1e8 cfu/mL suspension three weeks after emergence and again ~3 weeks later, exactly 72 h before Forl). Forl: 30 mL of 4e6 conidia/mL poured near each plant + razor crown wound. 6 plants per pathogen/endophyte combination (p4 2.7.3). Assessed 45 days after inoculation (uprooted, sectioned): incidence % infected plants, vascular discoloration length cm (Table 5 p15). Water-mock wounded control described in Methods but no data reported. No layout stated; individual plants are the units.
system: growth chamber, 2 L pots, commercial potting substrate

description: In vivo biocontrol vs Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans NCPPB4321 (Xep, bacterial spot), growth chamber, cv. Moneymaker in 2 L pots. Pathogen-inoculated untreated Control + 10 single-strain endophyte treatments (seed soaking 30 min + 50 mL soil drench of 1e8 cfu/mL three weeks after emergence and again ~3 weeks later, exactly 24 h before Xep). Xep spray-inoculated at 1e8 cfu/mL + 0.01% Tween 20. 6 plants per combination (p4 2.7.3). Assessed 6 days after inoculation: incidence (% symptomatic leaflets) and severity (% leaf area affected, ImageJ ~10 leaflets) (p5; Table 5 p15). Water negative control described in Methods but no data reported.
system: growth chamber, 2 L pots, commercial potting substrate

description: Unstressed growth-promotion assay on nursery plantlets, completely randomized block design (p5 2.7.4), cv. Moneymaker, growth chamber. Water-drench Control + 10 single strains, each 20 mL bacterial suspension (1e8 cfu/mL, p4 2.7.1) by soil drench immediately after transplant (Table 6 footnote; Fig 9 caption). Seven replicates per treatment. Height T0-T4 (Fig 9, context); after four weeks seedlings uprooted, shoot and root fresh and dry (70 C, 3 d) weights (Table 6 p17). Block design treated as independent parallel allocation (no shared cluster).

Greenhouse pot experiment (completely randomized design), tomato cv. SV4224TH, two seedlings per 14 x 13 cm pot (1:1 sand:peat), 5 pots per treatment; soil drench of 10 mL Bacillus paranthracis Endo10 (OD600 1.0, 1e7 CFU/mL) per pot followed 1 day later by 20 mL NaCl solution at 0, 100, 150 or 200 mM; ddH2O control; growth traits incl. plant fresh/dry weight measured 7 days after inoculation. Complete 4 salt x 2 inoculation factorial (8 arms).

Greenhouse pot experiment, tomato cv. Optima, IPBGR Thermi-Thessaloniki, May-Aug 2023: 3 drought levels (ND 85% FC, MDS 63.75% FC, SDS 42.5% FC) x 3 foliar treatments (distilled-water control, B1 BioElite 150 mL/ha, B2 Alga 600 1000 g/ha; 4 applications); two-factor split-plot (drought main plot, biostimulant subplot of 5 plants) in RCBD with 3 replicates; 6 weekly harvests.
system: GREENHOUSE_POT (6 L pots, 3:1 peat-perlite, drip irrigation, polyethylene greenhouse)

description: Screening trial: mock (MgSO4) vs 41 cold-tolerant bacterial endophyte isolates, single inoculation factor, 28 days at 25 +/- 2 C in growth chamber, no stress; 4 replicates (pool of 4 plants); shoot FW and DW (Fig 1, p4; Methods 4.2-4.3, p15).
system: growth chamber pots (45 cm3), twice-sterilized peat:sand 1:2, 25 +/- 2 C, 14:10 h photoperiod

description: Validation trial: mock vs 10 selected isolates x temperature regime (25 +/- 2 C non-stress vs 10 +/- 2 C cold, 14 d after 14 d at 25 C); full 11 x 2 crossed design; 4 replicates (pool of 7 plants); shoot FW and DW at end of incubation (Fig 2, p5; Methods p15).
system: growth chamber pots (45 cm3), twice-sterilized peat:sand 1:2, 14 d at 25 C then 14 d at 25 C or 10 C in separate chambers, 14:10 h photoperiod

description: Functional characterization trial: mock, Chryseobacterium sp. GRCS301, Pseudomonas sp. GRCS202 x temperature regime (25 C vs 10 C for 14 d after 14 d at 25 C); 3 replicates (pool of 7 plants) per condition and timepoint; shoot FW at 14 DAS, H2O2 at 1 DAS, RNA-Seq at 1 and 14 DAS; no dry weight (Fig 3, p5; Methods 4.3, p15-16).
system: growth chamber pots (45 cm3), twice-sterilized peat:sand 1:2, 14 d at 25 C then 14 d at 25 C or 10 C in separate chambers, 14:10 h photoperiod

description: Single greenhouse pot trial, University of Tuscia Experimental Farm, Viterbo, Italy, 20 Feb-5 Jul 2024; tomato cv Pralyna in 9 L pots (sandy loam 70% sand/30% soil), 3.5 plants/m2, pruned at eighth truss, drip fertigation EC 2.0. Full 2 x 3 factorial: irrigation W (well-watered, probe 50-80%) vs S (water-stressed, probe 30-50%) x biostimulant U (untreated, distilled water) vs PH-F (Malvaceae-derived protein hydrolysate foliar spray 3 mL/L to complete wetting) vs PH-R (same PH solution, 100 mL root drench per pot), applied every 10 days from 20 DAT to end of trial. Randomized complete block design, 96 plants, 16 biological replicates (plants) per treatment; irrigation applied by sector (two double rows per irrigation level). Two-way ANOVA with interaction, Tukey HSD; means +/- SE.

Greenhouse pot trial (Methods 2.3-2.4, 2.8, 2.13; pp3-5; Fig. 5 p8): tomato cv. Pomodoro Rio Grande, 25-cm pots 3/4 filled with sterile 1:1 sand:peat; inoculation levels MC (NB-475 vehicle control), B1 Bacillus subtilis IS-41, B2 B. velezensis IS-20, B3 B. siamensis IS-5, B4 Priestia filamentosa IS-24 (each strain applied alone as seed bacterization + 100 ml 20-fold diluted culture drench at planting) fully crossed with 2 salinity levels (tap water vs 100 mM NaCl irrigation from week 4 after transplanting, six weeks). After 3 weeks 14 uniform pots per inoculation treatment were split into 7 control + 7 NaCl pots (labels WC, WC-NaCl, MC, MC-NaCl, B1-C ... B4-NaCl). Terminal destructive measurement after the six-week salt treatment: shoot length, shoot/root FW, shoot/root DW (80 C, 7 d), flowers/plant; no fruit harvest. Fig. 5 caption / 2.13: three independent experiments, each with five biological replicates (n = 5), mean +/- SD, Tukey HSD over the 12 treatments. The same trial's WC arms are mapped as E2 only because they lack the NB-475 vehicle (distinct background); E1 and E2 share one trial, timepoint and dependency cluster.

Water-control (WC) arms of the SAME greenhouse pot trial as E1 (Methods 2.3-2.4, pp3-4; Fig. 5 p8): non-bacterized seedlings (MgSO4-treated seeds) given 100 ml water at planting instead of the NB-475 vehicle; 7 pots tap water (WC) vs 7 pots 100 mM NaCl (WC-NaCl); same substrate, salt regime, terminal harvest and statistics as E1. Not an independent experiment; separated from E1 solely to keep a distinct nonfactor background (water vs vehicle drench) so that MC remains the unique matched control of B1-B4.

Greenhouse pot experiment, tomato cv. Super Chief seedlings (5-7 leaves) in cocopeat:perlite 3:1; 8 inoculation treatments (SPB control, SHA, SHB, SHC, 3A, 3B, 3C, 3D; root dip 1e9 CFU/mL for 60 min before planting) x 2 NaCl levels (0, 100 mM, started one week after inoculation); 5 replications; completely randomized block design; all traits sampled two weeks after salinity onset.

In vitro seedling assay (Fig. 1A): tomato seeds germinated 14 d in Petri dishes on 8% agar-water medium with or without broccoli extract, at 0 mM or 40 mM NaCl; total seedling fresh weight (mg), mean +/- SE, n = 30; t-test. Context only (no fruit yield, no dry biomass).
system: in vitro Petri dish, 8% agar-water medium, controlled conditions

description: Hydroponic adult-plant experiment (Methods 2.1; Fig. 2): seed priming (untreated control vs germination 14 d on agar with broccoli extract) x salinity (0 vs 80 mM NaCl added to Hoagland solution for 10 d after 2 d vermiculite + 20 d Hoagland); complete 2x2 factorial analysed by two-way ANOVA; terminal aerial and root FW/DW (n = 6, mean +/- SE), gas exchange, water relations, minerals, phenolics, RT-qPCR.
system: hydroponic Hoagland solution, growth chamber (16 h light/8 h dark, 25/20 C, RH 60/80%, PAR 400 umol m-2 s-1)

description: Normal-condition seedling experiment (no imposed stress): tomato 'Pink Crown 2' in 50-hole trays (peat:vermiculite 3:1), growth chamber 28/18 C day/night, 16/8 h, 60-100 umol m-2 s-1, RH 50% (Methods 2.1, p2); 'spring season', sampled at 3-leaf stage (Methods 2.4, p4), 30 DAG (Results 3.1, p5). Explicit 2 x 4 factorial (Fig. 1A, p3): water (distilled vs HRW) x biostimulant (none, MC, CE, E) = 8 arms CK-D, MC, CE, E, CK-H, HMC, HCE, HE; two-way ANOVA Bio x HRW + Duncan (Methods 2.10, p5). Foliar spray at 250 mL per tray; 'each treatment was replicated three times'; Fig. 1 n = 3-12 biological replicates. Separate arms (trays) per treatment, no unit shared between arms; plants likely subsampled within tray-level applications (pseudoreplication RoB concern, not between-arm dependence).
system: growth chamber; seedlings in 50-hole plug trays, peat:vermiculite 3:1

description: Heat-stress seedling experiment: tomato 'Pink Crown 2' in 50-hole trays (peat:vermiculite 3:1); heat regime per Methods 2.1 (p2) growth chamber 32/22 C day/night, 16/8 h, 60-100 umol m-2 s-1, RH 50% for 25 d, but per Results 3.2 (p5) solar greenhouse 35/25 C day/night for 42 d (unresolved source discrepancy); 'summer season', sampled at 4-leaf stage (Methods 2.4). Separate experiment from E1 with its own controls (different season, regime, facility per Results, stage and duration): no common background with E1 and no unstressed control within this background. Explicit 2 x 4 factorial (Fig. 4 caption, p8; two-way ANOVA Bio x HRW): water (distilled vs HRW) x biostimulant (none, MC, CE, E) = 8 arms; Fig. 4 n = 12 biological replicates per treatment. Separate arms (trays), no unit shared between arms; within-tray subsampling is a RoB concern only.
system: growth chamber (Methods 2.1) vs solar greenhouse (Results 3.2), source discrepancy; seedlings in 50-hole plug trays, peat:vermiculite 3:1

description: Salt experiment: 2x2 factorial, Enterobacter sp. SA187 seed coating (none vs 10^6 CFU/ml, 1 h) x salinity (none vs 200 mM NaCl via pot trays for 15 days starting ~5 weeks after germination), tomato cv. Roma in peat moss pots under controlled greenhouse conditions (21-24/16-18 C, 60-70% RH, 16 h light); 3 biological replicates per treatment, CRD, one-way ANOVA + Tukey HSD; single destructive harvest of leaves and roots after 15 days of salt (Methods 2.1-2.2, 2.7; Fig. 1).

Heat experiment, conducted separately from E1 (Methods 2.2): plants with or without SA187 seed coating exposed to 42 C for 2 h in a growth chamber; leaves collected immediately; leaf/root fresh weight and leaf dry weight reported for WSA/H and SA/H only (Fig. 1c,d). No non-heated control set described for this experiment; WSA/C and SA/C of E1 are not verified as shared controls. 3 biological replicates per treatment, SD error bars.
system: Pot (sterilized peat moss), greenhouse-grown, heat shock in growth chamber

description: Greenhouse pot experiment, tomato cv. Shouhe, full 2x2x2 factorial R. irregularis CGMCC12157 (+/-) x T. harzianum CFCC82908 (+/-) x F. oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici (+/-); 9 pots per treatment (72 pots, RCBD), 2 plants per pot pooled; single destructive harvest 80 d after Fo inoculation.

In planta pot experiment (Methods 2.6-2.7, p3): tomato cv. BARI Tomato-2 in 30 cm plastic pots with autoclaved soil, kept under field conditions, Nov 2023-May 2024, Plant Pathology Division, BINA, Mymensingh, Bangladesh. Four treatments: uninoculated control (T0), F. oxysporum spray inoculation 3 weeks after transplanting (T3), T. asperellum soil inoculum 10^6 conidia/g soil at 4:1 soil:inoculum at transplanting (T1), and T. asperellum + F. oxysporum (T2). Three replicates of three seedlings per treatment. Outcomes: leaf disease incidence (%DI/PDI) at 0, 7, 14, 21 d post-inoculation and AUDPC (S and SB arms only, Fig. 5); leaf qRT-PCR expression (not a target).
system: POT_OUTDOOR_FIELD_CONDITIONS (30 cm plastic pots, autoclaved soil, plants kept under field conditions)

description: In planta growth-chamber assay: 25-d-old Saladette tomato seedlings (200-cavity trays, COSMO-PEAT; Conviron GEN2000 at 25 C, 80% RH, 12 h light), roots trimmed by one-third and dipped 15 min in F. solani conidia 1x10^6 mL-1 (or distilled water for control) before transplanting; chitosan 1/2/3 g L-1 sprayed to root collar and leaves 24 h before inoculation; carbendazim + F. solani chemical reference; maintained 28 C, 80% RH, 12 h light for 28 d. Completely randomised design, six plants per treatment, experiment repeated twice (pooling not stated). Outcomes at 28 d: plant height, stem diameter, dry root biomass, root length (Table 1), DS% and DI% (Fig 4), biocontrol efficacy (Fig 5), leaf SOD/CAT/POX/PAL (Table 2).

Greenhouse ('semi-field') pot experiment, Botany Department greenhouse, Mansoura University, Egypt: tomato Hybrid K 186 transplanted at 35 days into sterilized clay:sand (2:1) soil, superphosphate 0.6 g/pot; soil inoculation with Fusarium oxysporum (1 g sand-cornmeal inoculum per 100 g soil) in TO+ and T1-T6; single foliar spray of SA (0.5, 0.6 mM), HA (100, 150 mg/L) or ZnO-NPs (250, 500 mg/L) on the 40th day; 8 treatments, RCBD, 3 replicate pots x 5 plants (n = 15 plants per treatment); sampling of 70-day-old plants at early fruiting stage; disease assessed 36 days post-inoculation. No uninoculated biostimulant-only arms (not a factorial).

In vivo microplot experiment, Division of Nematology, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi: tomato cv. Pusa Ruby (21-day-old seedlings, 5 per plot) in M. incognita-infested microplots, 18 treatments (organic amendments, FYM-enriched Bacillus PGPR talc/liquid/consortium, botanical oils/hexane extracts at 1000 and 2000 ppm, Velum Prime chemical positive control, untreated), CRBD with 3 replicate plots per treatment, observations at 30, 60 and 90 days after transplanting; plants uprooted at 90 days.

Growth-room pot experiment (9x9x9.5 cm pots, 750 g autoclaved 75% sandy + 25% field soil), tomato SC-2121, completely randomized design with 6 treatments x 5 independent replicate pots: T. harzianum Rifai T22 bioproduct (TRIANUM P, WG, soil-incorporated before transplanting) at 30/40/50 g da-1 under M. incognita (1,000 J2/pot), abamectin nematicide reference under M. incognita, Control(+) nematode only, Control(-) no nematode; destructive harvest day 70.

Petri-dish seedling growth assay (Methods 2.2, Fig. 2): S. lycopersicum cv. Ailsa Craig seeds on 20 ml 1/2 MS medium supplemented with control, Fe3O4 NPs 0.5 or 1.0 mg/L, or FeCl3 0.53 or 1.06 mg/L; 3 dishes x 10 seeds per treatment; 25 C, 16/8 h; shoot length, root length, root-hair number after 8 d; repeated three times, one representative repetition shown (n = 10 seedlings). No stress. Context only.

Hydroponic Fusarium wilt experiment (Methods 2.4, Fig. 4): 20-d-old cv. Ailsa Craig seedlings in half-strength Hoagland (pH 5.8, replaced every two days), 2 L container with three seedlings, Fe treatments in the nutrient solution (FeCl3 0.53/1.06 mg/L, Fe3O4 NPs 0.5/1.0 mg/L) plus untreated, all spray-inoculated with Fol cfcc 80913 (1e8 CFU/ml, 30 s); grown 10 d at 25 C high humidity; three replicates per treatment; AUDPC from 1-5 wilt scale. No uninoculated arm reported.

Greenhouse pot assay, NARC-NPPRC Nepal, 22 Apr-27 Jun 2022: tomato cv. Pusa Ruby in 1 kg pots (steam-sterilized sandy soil:cocopeat:compost 5:1:1 + lime/DAP/MOP; autoclaved soil), 26 treatments = 22 native Trichoderma isolates (each + 2000 M. incognita J2) + non-inoculated control + J2-only control + fipronil chemical control + Nemastin commercial T. harzianum biological control; completely randomized design, three replicates per treatment, 'The experiment was repeated three times'; destructive sampling at 65 days post-transplant (p3 sec 2.4; Table 2 p5). No Trichoderma-without-J2 arm: not factorial.
system: greenhouse pot (1 kg pot, sterilized soil mix)

description: Greenhouse pot trial (25 +/- 2 C), tomato cv. Regina di Fasano, 1 L clay pots (14 cm diameter) of non-sterilized loam vineyard soil (Trani, Apulia) artificially infested with M. incognita (~7 eggs+J2 per mL soil); 8 treatments x 8 replicate pots: untreated infested control (CTR-t), fluopyram nematicide reference (CTV-t), and native or bioprocessed spent coffee grounds, brewers' spent grain and wasted bread at 3,000 kg OC/ha incorporated 2 weeks before transplanting; plants grown 2 months after transplanting, then uprooted for height, aerial and root dry weight, root gall index and eggs+J2 per g root.
system: greenhouse pot (1 L clay pots, non-sterilized infested soil)

description: In planta greenhouse pot trial (Fasano, Brindisi province, Italy; cv. DRW 7749 F1 indeterminate; 8 L pots, clay soil; randomised block design; 15 plants per group). Water stress (none / irrigation withheld to 25% soil moisture during fruit set of the second flowering, from 69 DAT, 11 days) crossed with MOF regimen (none / foliar 3 mL/L every 10 d / soil drench 200 mL of 3 mL/L every 10 d; MOF arms root-dipped 3 min in 7 mL/L at transplanting). Six groups T0-T5. Production: fruit set (%) and fruit cluster weight (g) at first flowering (non-stressed groups) and second flowering (stressed groups) (Fig 10, p12).

Seed priming germination assay (cv. Thonyno F1): seeds primed 24 h in MOF 3 mL/L vs water, then 3 Petri plates x 15 seeds per treatment at 21 C, 16/8 h; germination % (days 1-4) and root length (cm) (Methods 2.3 p3; Fig 3 p9). No stress; context only, no TFM target.

Greenhouse pot experiment (unheated greenhouse, Univ. Naples Federico II, Portici, Italy; transplant May 18, year not stated; 47 days, vegetative stage). Fully factorial 2x2: NaCl 1 mM (control) vs 75 mM in modified Hoagland solution x Chlamydomonas reinhardtii aqueous extract 0 g/L (A0, water) vs 4 g/L (A4), six weekly foliar sprays from 12 DAT (May 30). 3 replicates per treatment, 4 plants per replicate; two-way ANOVA (T, M, TxM) + Tukey HSD. Terminal dry biomass in Table 1 p4.
system: GREENHOUSE_POT (20 cm pots, peat:vermiculite 4:1, nutrient solution)

description: Tomato (S. lycopersicum var. cerasiforme) seedling growth-chamber pot experiment, March 2025, 27 days: full factorial of biostimulant inoculation (none / A Bacnifos / B Vibacter, each 5 L/ha-equivalent at day 0 and day 7) x water regime (80% FC well-watered / 40% FC water-stressed). 9 single-seedling 2 L pots per combination. Terminal shoot dry biomass at day 27. Maize arms of the same chamber experiment are out of scope.
system: Growth chamber, pots (2 L, commercial SIRO substrate with slow-release NPK 18-9-18), one seedling per pot

description: 2021 spring-summer campaign, polyethylene greenhouse IHSM La Mayora, Algarrobo (Malaga, Spain); tomato hybrid Macizo F1 in 17 L pots, single stem; full factorial irrigation (OIC vs SOIC = 60% of OIC from 14 DAT) x foliar treatment (mock diluted MS + 1.5 mM glucose/fructose vs T. harzianum CECT 2413 cell-free CF at D1 non-diluted, D2 1:2, D3 1:4; four applications); 10 plants per irrigation x treatment randomly set; fruit number, marketable yield (kg/plant, trusses 1-6) and mean fruit weight in Fig. 1 (mean +/- SD, n=10 individual plants).
system: Greenhouse pot (17 L, peat:coconut fibre:vermiculite 45:45:10), fertigation one emitter per plant

description: 2022 spring-summer campaign, same greenhouse, cultivar and pot system; full factorial irrigation (OIC vs SOIC = 60% of OIC from 14 DAT) x foliar treatment (mock diluted MS + 1.5 mM glucose/fructose vs T. harzianum CECT 2413 CF D2 1:2 only; four applications); 28 plants per irrigation x treatment randomly set; yield (Suppl. Figs 1-2) and terminal leaf/stem/root dry weight of 4 plants per arm (Suppl. Fig. 5) are only in unregistered supplements.
system: Greenhouse pot (17 L, peat:coconut fibre:vermiculite 45:45:10), fertigation one emitter per plant

description: Tomato growth-chamber pot experiment (Methods 2.4, PDF p5; Results 3.3.1, PDF p8-10; Supplementary Table S4): 29 inoculation levels (non-inoculated control C receiving three sterile PDA discs + 28 single endophytic fungal isolates BC01-BC52 of Table 1) x 2 salinity levels (N non-saline; S 100 mM NaCl irrigation from 15 DAS), one plant per 300 mL pot (two seedlings thinned to one), completely randomized design with 20 replicates per treatment, single destructive harvest after 42 days of salt treatment. Two-way ANOVA isolate (I) x salinity (S) stated in Methods 2.6 (PDF p6) and Figure 6 caption (PDF p10). Wheat pot trial, tomato/wheat germination plate assays and in vitro fungal growth assays are not mapped.
system: Growth chamber, 25 +/- 2 C, 16 h light/8 h dark, 60-70% RH; 300 mL pots with non-sterilized commercial peat-based substrate

description: Single greenhouse pot experiment, Utah State University (18 Dec 2024-21 Feb 2025), tomato Sunbrite F1. Explicit factorial: 7 biostimulant treatments (B, M, B+M, S+H, B+S+H, M+S+H, untreated control C) x 2 irrigation regimes (Full vs Deficit = 50% less water for 7 days, Day 58-65). RCBD, 5 blocks; 4 plants per biostimulant per block, split 2/2 between irrigation regimes at Day 58; n = 10 plants (2 x 5 blocks) per biostimulant x irrigation cell, 140 experimental units (one plant per pot). Biostimulants applied 3 times (Day 40, 47, 54; 27 Jan, 3 Feb, 10 Feb 2025) as root-zone drench in 50 mL water; control received water only. Terminal destructive harvest Day 65 (21 Feb 2025): shoot and root dry mass (60 C, 48 h). Two-way ANOVA with block random. Vegetative stage; no fruit yield measured.
system: greenhouse pot (8.5 x 8.5 x 8 cm pots, 300 g calcined clay substrate)

description: Greenhouse pot experiment, Shaqra, Saudi Arabia: tomato in 10 L pots with sterilized sand:peat (2:1 v/v), 25-28 C day / 18-20 C night, 60-70% RH; 2x2 crossing of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici Fo-QS1 inoculation (1e6 conidia/ml, root dip or soil drench 7 d after bacterial application) and Bacillus subtilis BS-QS1 (1e8 CFU/ml root dip 30 min before transplanting + soil drench 14 DAT); four treatments (Control, Fusarium, B. subtilis, B. subtilis + Fusarium) in an RCBD with 8 blocks (greenhouse position), one pot per treatment per block. Growth/DW after 30 days; yield components and total yield per plant at harvest.

Set 1 (Fig 2, Results 3.1 p5-6): TSWV isolate BPI-479 sap-inoculated tomato 'Belladonna F1' in insect-proof greenhouse; water control vs bacterial PGPMs Pseudomonas putida Z13, Paraburkholderia eburnea EP3, Bacillus velezensis K165 by root drench (3 weekly applications from BBCH 102, inoculation 1 day after 2nd application). Outcomes: disease severity index distribution (Fig 2B, 20 dpi, Chi-square) and DAS-ELISA OD415 apical non-inoculated leaves (Fig 2C, 20 dpi, ANOVA/Bonferroni). All arms inoculated; no uninoculated arm.

Set 2 (Fig 3, Results 3.1 p6-7): TSWV BPI-479 sap-inoculated 'Belladonna F1' in greenhouse; water control vs yeast isolate SRL248 by root drench (SRL248-D) or foliar spray (SRL248-S), 3 weekly applications from BBCH 102. Outcomes: severity index distribution (Fig 3A, 21 dpi), DAS-ELISA OD415 (Fig 3B, 21 dpi), plant height (Fig 3C, time not stated). All arms inoculated; own water control.

Set 3 (Fig 4A, Results 3.2 p7): CMV isolate I17-F sap-inoculated 'Belladonna F1' in greenhouse; water control vs Z13, EP3, K165 and Serifel (B. amyloliquefaciens MBI600) by root drench. Outcome: DAS-ELISA OD415 at 14 dpi; symptoms reported as not different among treatments (no data). All arms inoculated.

Set 4 (Fig 4B, Results 3.2 p7-8): CMV I17-F sap-inoculated 'Belladonna F1' in greenhouse; water control vs SRL248 root drench (SRL248-D) or foliar spray (SRL248-S). Outcome: DAS-ELISA OD415 at 14 dpi (p = 0.947). Own water control, separate from Fig 4A.

Set 5 (Fig 4C, Results 3.2 p8): ToBRFV-Gr sap-inoculated 'Belladonna F1' in greenhouse; water control vs K165 and Serifel by root drench. Outcome: DAS-ELISA OD415 at 11 dpi (p = 0.07); symptoms similar among treatments at 5 dpi (no data).

Set 6 (Methods 2.5 p5, Fig 5 p9): growth chamber (Panasonic MLR-352H) gene-expression experiment, no virus inoculation; water control vs Serifel, K165, Z13, EP3 by root drench; SlPR1b.1 and SlRdR1 RT-qPCR in upper leaf at 24 h after the 2nd drench (just prior to the would-be inoculation); 5 plants per treatment; error bars 2 x SE. CONTEXT only (transcript markers, not a target).

Botrytis greenhouse experiment, whole-plant growth: tomato cv. Moneymaker transplanted on day 14 into 1 L pots of sterilized vermiculite:coarse sand (1:1), greenhouse 20-25 C, 16 h light, 65% RH, Kristalon 18-18-18 fertigation; root-zone soil inoculation on day 14 with 1 mL of 10^8 CFU/mL K. radicincitans DSM 16656 or P. phytofirmans PsJN, or 1 mL 10 mM MgCl2 mock. Whole plants were never pathogen-challenged. Growth (shoot/root fresh and dry weight per plant, shoot length, leaf number) recorded after a 30-day colonization period (day 44), n=10 plants per treatment (2.3.2, Fig 4). One-way comparison of three independent arms.

Botrytis detached-leaf bioassay on the E1 plants: terminal three leaflets of the 4th true leaf detached on day 44 from 5 plants per bacterial treatment and challenged with two 5 mm Gamborg B5 plugs per leaflet carrying 10 uL of 10^6 germinated B. cinerea DSM 4709 conidia/mL; incubated 72 h at 21 C, constant light, 70% RH; lesion diameter (mean of longest/shortest, ImageJ) and necrosis severity class (mild/moderate/severe) scored at 3 dpi (day 47) (2.3.3, Figs 5-6, Table S4). All reported arms are pathogen-challenged; n=30 plug lesions per arm are pseudoreplicates nested in 15 leaflets nested in 5 plants. Leaflets come from the same plants as E1 (shared plants).
system: detached leaflet assay in climate chamber (leaflets from greenhouse pot plants)

description: Fusarium greenhouse experiment: explicit 3 x 2 factorial of bacterial inoculation (10 mM MgCl2 mock / K. radicincitans DSM 16656 / P. phytofirmans PsJN, 1 mL of 10^8 CFU/mL to soil on day 14) x pathogen challenge (5 min root-dip of trimmed roots, ~1 cm left, on day 24 in 10^7 spores/mL F. oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici FOL 029 race 3, or in autoclaved heat-killed FOL spore suspension as mock), then potted in 1 L pots for a 3-week challenge period; six treatments listed in 2.4.2; n=4 plants per cell; growth (shoot/root fresh and dry weight, height, leaves, plant fresh weight), disease index 0-5, and FOL re-isolation from root and stem nodes at day 45 (21 days post-challenge; outgrowth read on day 47). Two-way factorial ANOVA with factors B and P (Figs 8-10, Table S5).

Greenhouse pot experiment, tomato cv. Farmers 301 (FOL race 2 susceptible), complete 2 x 3 x 2 factorial: silicon (2 mM K2SiO3 20 mL/pot at transplanting vs KCl potassium balance) x soil-drench bacterium (dH2O, Burkholderia contaminans NRBC, Burkholderia sp. NRBA; 10 mL of 1e8 CFU/mL at 2 DAT plus reapplication with 20-fold diluted cell-free culture broth at 9 DAT) x Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici race 2 Foly4 (10 mL of 1e6 spores/mL after root wounding at 10 DAT vs 0.05% Tween20 mock). 12 groups, >= 5 single-plant pots per group per trial, CRD, entire experiment repeated four times and pooled. Outcomes at 21 dppi (growth incl. shoot and root dry weight), disease incidence 14/21 dppi, severity 8-21 dppi, AUDPC, FOL re-isolation.

Single greenhouse / climate-chamber pot experiment on tomato cv. Matin F1 (Plant Virology Research Center, Shiraz University, Iran). Six treatments in a completely randomized design, all TYLCV-inoculated with viruliferous Bemisia tabaci (5 adults/plant, 72 h inoculation access period, 24 h after the second foliar spray): B. subtilis PVRC001 encapsulated in chitosan-Persian gum complexes made with ~20 kDa (ULMWCC), ~50 kDa (LMWCC), ~150 kDa (MMWCC) or ~1250 kDa (HMWCC) chitosan; non-encapsulated B. subtilis PVRC001 (BS); and an untreated TYLCV-inoculated control sprayed with sterile distilled water. One shared control for all five treated arms. No non-inoculated arm and no carrier-only (chitosan-Persian gum without bacteria) arm, so this is an S vs S+B design and not a factorial. Methods p3 (receipt SRC-125c67457d1530023f828a18).
system: greenhouse/climate-chamber pot (12 x 10 cm pots, one plant per pot, autoclaved substrate)

description: TYLCV agro-inoculation (A. tumefaciens C58 MP90 carrying TYLCV infectious clone, OD600 = 1, ~50 uL infiltrated into three leaflets per plant, one day after second drench); Water vs MBI600 drench, both inoculated; symptoms (Fig 1A, 20 and 25 dpi photos) and TYLCV DNA copies/ng DNA by qPCR at 20 dpi (Fig 1B) and 32 dpi (Fig 1C). n per group, layout and randomization not stated.
system: insect-proof greenhouse, pots 90x90x100 mm, soilless Potgrond P

description: TYLCV transmission by viruliferous Bemisia tabaci MED (50 per cage, 72 h IAP) at the 2nd-3rd true leaf stage; per run one insect-proof cage of 10 MBI600-treated plants and one cage of 10 water-treated plants; repeated three times (30 plants per treatment). Symptom progression 10-70 dpi every 2 days (Fig 2A, average symptomatic plants per 10-plant cage over 3 runs) and TYLCV qPCR Cq at 14 and 28 dpi on the same plants (Fig 2B; LMM with plant random effect; text deltaCq at 14 dpi). Treatment confounded with cage.
system: insect-proof screen cages in insect-proof greenhouse, pots 90x90x100 mm

description: CMV-I17F mechanical (sap) inoculation with carborundum on one leaflet of the upper fully expanded leaf, one day after second drench; Water vs MBI600, both inoculated; performed twice, 30 plants per treatment; symptoms and DAS-ELISA in apical non-inoculated leaves. Results in prose only (no significant differences).
system: insect-proof greenhouse, pots 90x90x100 mm, soilless Potgrond P

description: TSWV-619 mechanical (sap) inoculation as for CMV; Water vs MBI600, both inoculated; Methods state performed twice with 30 plants per treatment, but no TSWV phenotypic result is reported in this article (design record only).
system: insect-proof greenhouse, pots 90x90x100 mm, soilless Potgrond P

description: CONTEXT ONLY. RNA-seq sampling T0 (just prior to virus inoculation, one day after the second drench), growth chamber; Water vs MBI600, 3 plants per group; upper leaf transcriptome (Table 1: 0 DEGs).
system: growth chamber MLR-352H Panasonic, 16 h light, 25/22 C, RH 85/90%

description: CONTEXT ONLY. RNA-seq at 3 dpi after sap inoculation: Mock (phosphate buffer), CMV, TSWV x Water/MBI600, 3 plants per group, upper non-inoculated fully expanded leaf; DEG counts vs Water-Mock (Table 1), Venn/GO/KEGG (Figs 3-5), RT-qPCR verification (Suppl. Table 3).
system: growth chamber MLR-352H Panasonic, 16 h light, 25/22 C, RH 85/90%

description: CONTEXT ONLY. RNA-seq at 5 dpi after agro-inoculation: Agro (empty binary vector) mock and TYLCV x Water/MBI600, 3 plants per group, upper non-inoculated fully expanded leaf; DEG counts vs Water-Agro (Table 1), Fig 3C, Suppl. Table 2.
system: growth chamber MLR-352H Panasonic, 16 h light, 25/22 C, RH 85/90%

description: Insect-free greenhouse pot experiment (sterile pots, 2:1 double-autoclaved soil:sand, 25+/-2 C, 16/8 h), completely randomized design: 2 cultivars (Moneymaker, Tabas) x 8 seed-priming treatments forming a complete 2x2x2 of BABA 10 mM, Bacillus subtilis A4 1e6 CFU/mL and Trichoderma zelobreve T20 1e9 CFU/mL (none, Ba, B, T, BaB, BaT, BT, BaBT; 3 h seed soak in 40 mL, microbes in 1% CMC, air-dried before sowing) x ToLCPalV (V0 non-inoculated; V1 agroinfiltrated DNA-A+DNA-B, OD600 0.2, 100 uL, 30-day-old two-true-leaf seedlings). Endpoints to 40 dpi (end of experiment). Conducted twice independently; pooled after non-significant experiment x treatment interaction; only pooled data reported.

In planta greenhouse pot experiment (Methods p3 'Nematicidal assay of organic acids under Greenhouse conditions' + Table 1 p3; receipt SRC-05df33f8307b00bc2e13a6a5): tomato cv. '023' seedlings transplanted to 2 kg plastic pots of autoclaved sandy loam; 9 treatments T1-T9 (T1 infected untreated positive control, T2 non-infected untreated negative control, T3 oxamyl pesticide reference, T4-T9 salicylic/citric/malic/lactic/benzoic/acetic acid on M. incognita-inoculated plants). OA: 500 mL of the lowest effective lab concentration per plant = 50 mg acid/plant (i.e. 0.01% w/v), soil drench; first application at transplanting, inoculation with ~2000 J2 in 5 mL 10 days after transplanting and OA application; OA applications repeated every two weeks, three in total. CRD, 27-32 C natural daylight, weekly Vascon 20-20-20 fertilization 2 g/L. Concluded 42 days after nematode inoculation (p4, receipt SRC-42177f3c3e006b2412fc9b1c). Replication: Methods p3 'Each treatment included ten replicates'; Table 4 (p6) and Table 5 (p7) captions 'Each mean value came from three replicates' (unresolved conflict, recorded as source limit).

Greenhouse pot trial (King Abdulaziz Univ., Dept. of Agriculture, Jeddah, 2021-2022), tomato cv. Doucen, 1 plant/pot (25 cm pots, peat:sandy loam 1:3). Complete 2x2x2 FOL x B. safensis HS-3 x DHCl factorial set of 8 randomly assigned treatments (T1-T8), CRD, n=6 replicates. Treatments applied 3 weeks after transplanting, FOL (1e8 conidia/mL, 10 mL/pot root zone) applied 24 h later. Disease severity at 60 d after treatments (Fig. 2A); shoot and root fresh/dry weight (Table 2, mean +/- SD, n=6).

Open-field trial (Hada Al-Sham Research Station, King Abdulaziz Univ., Jeddah), two consecutive winter growing seasons (printed as 2021-2022; Season-I and Season-II), tomato cv. Doucen, drip irrigation, natural FOL pressure. RCBD, 8 replicates x 6 plants per treatment. 4 arms: T1 naturally infected control (water spray), T2 B. safensis (root dip + soil drench at transplanting), T3 DHCl 100 uM foliar (at transplant and 2 weeks later), T4 DHCl + B. safensis. DS at 60 DAT (Fig. 7A); total fruit yield per plant at end of season (Fig. 7B, kg/plant, mean +/- SD, n=8).

Setup 1, seed soaking (Methods p.3): tomato varieties K-21 and S-22; seeds soaked 6 h in GABA 0 (control), 0.25, 0.5 or 0.75 mM and sown immediately in earthen nursery pots; transplanted 20 days after sowing into earthen pots (25x25 cm) with soil:farmyard manure 6:1 and basal N 40 mg, P 138 mg, K 26 mg kg-1; 150 mM NaCl through the soil at 20 DAT, five times at one-day interval; 8 treatments per variety (Control, GABA 0.25/0.5/0.75 mM, NaCl 150 mM, GABA 0.25/0.5/0.75 mM + NaCl) = 16 cells; assessed at 40 DAT. Factorial randomized design, net house, AMU Aligarh. Replication as printed: 'number of replicates for each treatment were five (n=5)'. Figures: mean +/- standard error, Tukey test.
system: Pot culture in net house (earthen pots 25x25 cm, soil:FYM 6:1; day 20-25 C, night 15-20 C, RH 60-70%)

description: Setup 2, foliar spray (Methods p.3): tomato varieties K-21 and S-22; surface-sterilized seeds sown in earthen nursery pots; seedlings transplanted after 20 days into earthen pots (25x25 cm), three plants per pot; 150 mM NaCl through the soil at 20 DAT on five alternating days; foliar GABA 0, 0.25, 0.5 or 0.75 mM at 30 DAT for 5 consecutive days in presence or absence of NaCl; 8 treatments per variety = 16 cells; evaluated at 40 DAT. Same factorial randomized net-house design. Replication as printed for setup 2: 'Each pot accommodated three plants'; no separate n is printed for setup 2 (n=5 appears only in the setup 1 paragraph) and the replicate unit (pot vs plant) is not stated. Figures: mean +/- standard error, Tukey test.
system: Pot culture in net house (earthen pots 25x25 cm, three plants per pot; day 20-25 C, night 15-20 C, RH 60-70%)

description: In vivo pot experiment (RCBD, 3 replicates per treatment) on tomato F1 hybrid 'Red Rose' seedlings in autoclaved clay:sand:peat (1:1:1), 200 g soil per pot: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici soil infestation (none/Fol) crossed with biocontrol agent (none / Pseudomonas putida seed bio-priming / Penicillium chrysogenum soil inoculum); six treatments C, FC, B, BF, P, PF; evaluated at 14, 21 and 28 days after sowing.

Main combined greenhouse experiment: 10-day-old WT MICRO-TOM and ethylene-insensitive Never ripe (Nr, MICRO-TOM background) seedlings in 1.5 L Leonard pots (vermiculite:sand 1:1, half-strength Hoagland) treated for 25 days with Control (nutritive solution), humic acid from vermicompost (HA 190.36 mg/L), NaCl 100 mM, or HA+NaCl; completely randomized; replicate = one pot with three plants; root morphology (Fig. 1), root and shoot dry biomass (Fig. 2), photochemistry (Fig. 3), antioxidant enzymes and Evans blue (Fig. 4); two-way ANOVA genotype x treatment.
system: greenhouse semi-hydroponic Leonard pots (1.5 L, vermiculite:sand 1:1, half-strength Hoagland)

description: Summer 2022 (9 Jun-16 Aug 2022) mesh-covered field container experiment, Centro de Experiencias Cajamar, Paiporta, Valencia, Spain; S. lycopersicum cv. Micro-Tom in single-plant 5 L containers (Terra Vagiota substrate:river sand 2:1, daily drip nutrient solution). Complete randomized block design, 8 treatments x 20 single-plant replicates (n=160): salinity (no stress vs 100 mM NaCl, 70 mL per pot, 46 days from 4 weeks after transplanting) x BS Calbio (no/yes) x P. megaterium BM08 (no/yes). Fruit yield (Fig. 1A per harvest R1-R4; Fig. 1B cumulative total) reported only under salt; terminal aerial and root dry weight (Supplementary Fig. 2B-C) for all 8 treatments.
system: mesh-covered open-field containers (5 L pots, one plant per container)

description: Field experiment Aug-Oct 2024, Huaiyin District, Jiangsu, China, natural bacterial-wilt (R. solanacearum) field; untreated control vs B. velezensis or P. fluorescens granules each at 1:500, 1:300, 1:150 dilution, root spray 50 mL/plant on 12, 15, 18 Sep; assessments 15 d after application (27 Sep).
